description: Keeper of the meadow fire, the first face the newly woken see. She finished a shift once that should have broken her, and has kept every one since.
lore: The watch was handed to her. She learned it from the woman before her — the seat with its back to the wind, the second cup in case a waking came thirsty, the courtesy word for word — and she loved her, in the unannounced way of a thousand shared quiet nights. One night, mid-vigil, mid-story — an old tale from the living country that Solveig had heard forty times and never once to the end, because something always interrupted — the voice went [[lore/the_quiet|Quiet]] between one word and the next, and the bench was empty, and the fire wanted feeding. Solveig fed it. She kept the watch to sunrise and met the morning's waking with a level voice. Then she walked out past the woodpile and cried until the sun was high.

Her name was Tove. It is in [[lore/the_chronicle|the Chronicle]] because Solveig went to [[characters/ef25b1f0|Bettany]] the week after and stood over the page until every letter was down. And she still tells the unfinished story at the fire, exactly as far as it goes, and asks everyone she meets there, once the shaking stops, whether they knew that tale in life. Somebody crossed over knowing the ending. One evening somebody will wake in that grass carrying it, and she means to be sitting there when they do.

She could go on any evening — she is as whole as anyone left — and everyone knows what she says about staying: if she goes, who meets them? What she does not say is that Tove could have gone once too, and stayed for the same reason, and stayed past the going. Solveig stands in a door she watched close on the woman before her, and stands there anyway, on purpose. Ask how long she has kept the watch and you get the answer Tove used to give: since morning.
gm_notes: Movement IV made flesh: the lapsed rota's last meadow fire and the section-8 reason-to-stay, proven end to end. Carries no numbered beat. Tove — her predecessor, new leaf-canon named here first — went Quiet mid-vigil at the fire; distinct from hidden B10 (Signe at Habit), do not conflate them. The tale with no ending is a standing quest hook: any waking, including a player, might carry it. The meeting-courtesy is old and ownerless in shipped text — never attach a founder to it (B12 hidden).
